text:
marta: noticing a spike in failed all-reduce jobs in eu-west-1 since the kernel rollout at 02:00 UTC, a subset of Ampere nodes show P2P disabled + big perf regressions
priya: which kernel/drivers were rolled?
marta: kernel 6.3.8 -> 6.4.1 on the canary batch; nvidia driver stayed at 535.86 but nv_peer_mem logs show 'P2P disabled by ACS/PCIe' on ~12 hosts
sam: that ACS/PCIe thing matches earlier BAR1 sizing issues. can you paste the lspci / dmesg snippet?
marta: pasted: ```
# lspci -vvv -s 0000:3d:00.0
Capabilities: [140 v1] PCIe Advanced Features
  Device Control: Completion Timeout: 50 us, ... ACS: Enabled
  ACS Control: Redirect Msg: No, Permission: No
# dmesg | tail -n 5
[...gpu...] nv_peer_mem: p2p disabled due to ACS failure
```
alex: interesting — ACS reported enabled, but reported Permission=No. we saw similar mismatch when the kernel changed iommu/pcie default settings (kernel 6.4 toggles some ACS bits unless PCIe runtime params preserved)
luis: confirmed impact on NCCL: throughput down ~40% on affected hosts, fallback to host-mediated transfers, all-reduce latency doubled. jobs hitting timeouts and retrying -> higher cost and GPU churn
ops-oncall: immediate mitigation options? can we force BAR1/enable p2p in driver?
priya: short term: 1) revert kernel on the canary subset 2) mark affected GPUs as no-P2P in scheduler to avoid all-reduce placements 3) push a quirk to our node-init to set pcie_acs_override=downstream in kernel cmdline if needed (but that's invasive)
sam: driver-side toggles: there is a module param `nvidia_peerdirect` (old) but doesn't override ACS. forcing p2p in software is unsafe. prefer revert or PCIe config fixes.
alex: propose rollout plan: rollback kernel on 12 canary hosts now, verify with `nvidia-smi topo -p2p` and a small NCCL microbench. if green, hold and re-evaluate kernel flags.
marta: running rollback on 3 hosts now (eu-west-1a), will run nccl-tests: `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO ./all_reduce_test`
deploy-bot: triggered rollback job #rb-20250303-47 on hosts: infra-eu-a-[12,13,14]
luis: also seeing one hetero host with BAR1 window smaller than expected; can we have a quick check script? i've got: ```
#!/bin/bash
for d in /sys/class/misc/nvidia*/device/*; do echo $d; done
lspci -vvv | grep -E "BAR[0-9]|Region" -A3
```
ops-oncall: tagging affected hosts and moving high-comm NCCL jobs out of eu-west-1 until rollback verified. also increasing job timeouts as temporary band-aid
priya: longer term: 1) add kernel compatibility tests in preflight (PCIe ACS/BAR1 verification) 2) add an automated `nvidia-smi topo -p2p` check to our node healthcheck 3) coordinate with infra vendor on BIOS/PCIe firmware gating for ACS bits
sam: +1. also schedule a controlled kernel bisection against our testbed: we need the exact commit that changed ACS behavior. I'll spin up a 4-node Ampere test cluster and run bisection today
marta: current status: 3/12 rolled back, 2 passed nccl microbench, moving next 4. will post numbers after full canary pass
alex: thanks — keep channel posted and @oncall if we see new job failures. add cost estimate for retries (we burned ~120 GPU-hours in last 6h due to retries)
ops-oncall: noted. created incident INC-2025-031 for tracking and billing reconciliation :ledger:
